name: LAYERS
tagline: Stats harness: rule-based vs graph AML detection on synthetic data

children.title: Data inputs
children.summary: Loads IBM's synthetic AML transaction CSV (or a generated dev fixture) into Postgres, then derives the account graph from it.
children.detail: Research on IBM's public synthetic data only, not real customers and not a production AML system. It scores an immutable historical corpus offline.

children.title: IBM HI-Small dataset
children.summary: IBM's synthetic anti-money-laundering transactions, the HI-Small variant. Downloaded separately, never committed to the repo.
children.detail: 5,078,345 transactions, 515,080 accounts, 0.102% laundering. Five other variants (HI/LI small, medium, large) already have table partitions waiting.

children.title: Synthetic dev fixture
children.summary: Generates a small CSV in the IBM format so the whole pipeline runs without the real data.
children.detail: Plants laundering as structure (cycles, fan-out bursts, layering chains) with amounts drawn from normal traffic, after an earlier version leaked the answer through round amounts. Fixture results are explicitly not findings.

children.title: Idempotent CSV ingest
children.summary: Bulk-loads the CSV into its variant partition. Re-running is a no-op, and a crashed run resumes where it stopped.

children.title: COPY to staging, cast in SQL
children.summary: Rows land as text in a temp staging table and Postgres does the type casts, which takes seconds instead of minutes of Python parsing.

children.title: Natural key on row number
children.summary: UNIQUE (dataset_variant, source_row_num) plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so loading twice never doubles the corpus.

children.detail: Reads columns by position (the IBM file has two columns both named Account) and commits every 100,000 rows so progress is durable.

children.title: Account graph build
children.summary: Derives accounts and directed edges from a variant's transactions. Dataset-scoped and safe to re-run.
children.detail: Edges carry totals, counts and average time between payments (computed with LAG). HI-Small yields 1,015,736 edges.

children.title: Postgres schema
children.summary: PostgreSQL 16 holds the corpus, run outputs, comparisons, the job queue and auth. Partitioned from day one.
children.detail: Idempotent DDL in schema.sql, with Alembic migrations 0001-0005 for later changes (run diagnostics, self-transactions, wider currency, matched rate).

children.title: Partitioned transactions
children.summary: Transactions are LIST-partitioned by dataset variant, so a second variant loads without a migration.
children.detail: A variant filter plans an index-only scan on one partition of six.

children.title: Per-run scores
children.summary: scores is HASH-partitioned by run (16 partitions). account_scores snapshots graph features per run so runs never overwrite each other.
children.detail: The original spec stored features on accounts, so a second run silently corrupted any comparison with the first. Logged as defect S2 and fixed.

children.title: Reproducible run records
children.summary: Each detection run stores config_hash, code_version and random_seed, with telemetry kept in a separate diagnostics column.

children.title: Comparisons + metrics
children.summary: A comparison row is the job; comparison_metrics holds one row per metric with CI, raw and adjusted p-values.
children.detail: CHECK blocks comparing a run to itself. p-values are DOUBLE PRECISION so values below 1e-8 don't round to zero.

children.title: Least-privilege roles
children.summary: Four Postgres roles. Grants, not code conventions, decide who can touch what, so a bug in a route can't exceed them.

children.title: layers_api
children.summary: Can validate, enqueue and read. Cannot write scores or any analytical table, cannot run DDL, 30s statement timeout.

children.title: layers_worker
children.summary: Writes scores and results but has no access at all to api_keys. Gets TEMPORARY for the ingest staging table.

children.detail: Also layers_readonly (no api_keys or audit_log) and layers_migrator (the only role that applies schema). None is superuser. The jobs, api_keys and audit_log tables live here too.

children.title: Job queue + worker
children.summary: Nothing long-running happens in a request. The API enqueues a row and workers claim it from Postgres, no broker needed.

children.title: SKIP LOCKED claims
children.summary: Workers claim with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, safe under any number of concurrent workers.

children.title: Heartbeats + orphan reclaim
children.summary: Running jobs heartbeat and write progress to their own row. A job whose worker died is returned to the queue.
children.detail: SIGTERM/SIGINT set a flag so the job in flight finishes and commits; a hard-killed worker leaves a stale heartbeat that gets reclaimed. Either way no job is silently lost.

children.title: Retries with backoff
children.summary: Failed jobs retry with exponential backoff up to max_attempts. Bad input fails permanently instead of looping.

children.title: Job handlers
children.summary: Four job types run in order for a full analysis: ingest, build_graph, detect, compare. Bad input fails fast and isn't retried.
children.detail: detect writes millions of score rows with COPY instead of executemany, which saves minutes per run. Job payloads are re-validated on claim, including path containment on the ingest filename.

children.title: Two detectors
children.summary: A four-rule baseline and a graph method, both pure functions over numpy arrays with no database or HTTP inside.
children.detail: Neither detector was tuned; both ran at documented defaults. Keeping the domain layer pure is what lets each one be tested against known answers.

children.title: Rule-based baseline
children.summary: Four independent rules. Score is rules fired / 4, flagged if any fired, with the rule names kept as reasons.
children.detail: Only five possible score values, so ranking metrics are tie-heavy for it. On HI-Small its AUC-ROC was 0.4967, basically a coin flip.

children.title: Large transaction
children.summary: Fires on amounts above a threshold (default 50,000).

children.title: Rapid succession
children.summary: Counts the sender's payments in a trailing time window using a SQL window function, one sort instead of a self-join.
children.detail: The original spec used a +/- window, twice as wide as documented and looking into the future. Fixed to a trailing window that includes the scored row.

children.title: Round amount
children.summary: Fires when an amount sits within a tolerance of a round multiple.

children.title: Cross-currency high value
children.summary: Fires when payment and receiving currency differ and the amount is above a threshold (default 10,000).

children.title: Five account features
children.summary: Degree ratio, cycle participation, temporal burst, pass-through ratio and log transaction count, in a fixed column order.

children.title: Degree ratio
children.summary: Out-degree over in-degree, stored as double precision so huge hubs don't overflow.

children.title: Cycle participation
children.summary: Whether an account sits on a money loop. Exact enumeration runs under a time budget, with an SCC fallback.
children.detail: Length-bounded simple_cycles still blew up on dense graphs, so a wall-clock budget switches to an O(V+E) strongly-connected-components check. Which method ran is recorded on the run.

children.title: Temporal burst
children.summary: Largest share of an account's activity inside any one time window, found with an O(n) two-pointer sweep.

children.title: Pass-through ratio
children.summary: How closely money in matches money out, a classic layering signal.

children.title: Log transaction count
children.summary: log1p of activity, so a handful of hyperactive accounts don't dominate every split in the forest.

children.title: Graph + Isolation Forest
children.summary: Builds five graph features per account, scores them with an unsupervised Isolation Forest, then maps account risk onto transactions.

children.title: Isolation Forest scoring
children.summary: Unsupervised anomaly model over the feature matrix, default 200 trees, fixed seed for reproducibility.
children.detail: Risk is a rank transform of the raw score, and flagged uses the same quantity, so the two can never disagree. A known-answer test caught an inverted sort that would have flagged the most ordinary accounts.

children.title: Account-to-transaction map
children.summary: A transaction is flagged if either its sender or receiver account is flagged, so both detectors score the same rows.

children.title: Flagged network extraction
children.summary: Bounded 2-hop ego networks around flagged accounts, highest risk first, with a size cap and a truncated flag.
children.detail: The original spec unioned ancestors and descendants, which on a giant component is basically the whole 515k-node graph.

children.title: Statistical evaluation
children.summary: Compares two runs on five metrics, each with a 95% CI on the difference and a corrected p-value, picking the right test per metric.
children.detail: 10,000 bootstrap replicates over 5.08M transactions finish in about 0.5 seconds, because the naive row-resampling bootstrap would never finish.

children.title: Run alignment check
children.summary: Refuses to compare runs that scored different data: variant, row count and transaction set must match, else 409.

children.title: 8-cell multinomial bootstrap
children.summary: Precision, recall and F1 CIs from resampling an 8-cell count table instead of millions of rows. Two-sided p-values.

children.title: DeLong test
children.summary: Closed-form paired test for AUC-ROC with midrank tie handling. Matches sklearn's AUC to about 1e-16.

children.title: Stratified AUC-PR bootstrap
children.summary: Paired bootstrap for average precision over a presorted score order, scaling with positives rather than corpus size.

children.title: Stratified McNemar
children.summary: Exact McNemar run separately on true positives and flagged negatives, since pooled accuracy is swamped by easy negatives.

children.title: Multiple-comparison fix
children.summary: Benjamini-Hochberg or Holm adjustment across the five metrics, so testing five things doesn't inflate false wins.

children.title: Matched flag rate
children.summary: Re-thresholds the graph score to the rule detector's flag rate for a like-for-like comparison. Records if the rate was hit exactly.
children.detail: The Isolation Forest's contamination knob pins its flag rate. At a matched 29.8% rate, the recall gap flipped from -0.09 to +0.18.

children.title: The finding
children.summary: Graph method ranks better (AUC-ROC +0.120) but both detectors are near-useless here: precision ~0.001, about 999 false alarms per hit.
children.detail: All five differences are significant, mostly because n is five million. The write-up leads with effect sizes and CIs, and says this is about these two untuned detectors on one synthetic dataset.

children.title: REST API
children.summary: FastAPI service that authenticates, validates, enqueues and reads results. Every number it serves was already computed by a worker.

children.title: Runs endpoints
children.summary: POST /api/runs returns 202 and queues a run; GET shows status with live stage progress; runs can be cancelled.

children.title: Comparisons endpoints
children.summary: Create a comparison (202) then poll it, same shape as runs, so no bootstrap ever runs inside a request.

children.title: Networks + accounts
children.summary: Paginated flagged networks and flagged accounts per run, plus a single-network fetch for the graph view.

children.title: Strict request validation
children.summary: Every numeric field is bounded and extra fields are rejected, with method-based config dispatch.
children.detail: Fixes a spec bug where a graph config silently parsed as a rule config, dropping every graph parameter with no error.

children.title: Middleware stack
children.summary: API-key auth with read/write scopes, per-key rate limits, audit logging, request IDs and one error envelope for every failure.

children.title: React frontend
children.summary: React 19 + Vite app to launch runs, compare them and explore flagged networks. No UUID pasting anywhere.

children.title: Plain-language verdict
children.summary: Leads the comparison with a sentence generated from the data, and deliberately refuses to just say 'X wins'.

children.title: Forest plot
children.summary: Shows each metric's difference with its CI against zero, faceted by scale so tiny metrics aren't flattened.

children.title: D3 network view
children.summary: Force-directed graph of a flagged network. Risk rides node size, flagged status uses color plus a legend.

children.title: Generated API client
children.summary: Types are generated from OpenAPI and never hand-edited. CI fails if they drift from the backend.

children.title: Security
children.summary: Threat model focused on compute abuse and result integrity, with a per-milestone checklist. 46 of 50 controls done.

children.title: Hashed API keys
children.summary: 256-bit random keys shown once, SHA-256 at rest, constant-time comparison, identical 401s so errors can't be used as an oracle.

children.title: nginx edge
children.summary: Per-IP rate limit, 64k body cap, CSP and other security headers. Only the UI publishes a port.

children.title: Hardened containers
children.summary: Non-root (uid 10001), read-only root filesystem, capabilities dropped, base images pinned by digest.
children.detail: The internet-facing API image is built without scikit-learn, and CI fails if it shows up there.

children.title: Supply-chain checks
children.summary: Hash-pinned lockfiles with a drift check, pip-audit for known vulnerabilities and Bandit static analysis in CI.
children.detail: A secret scanner also runs in a pre-commit hook and again in CI over full git history, and config refuses placeholder passwords at startup.

children.title: Backup restore drill
children.summary: Dumps, restores into a throwaway database and compares row counts table by table. Passed on the full corpus.

children.title: Tests + CI
children.summary: Known-answer tests for the stats, integration tests against real Postgres, and a seven-job GitHub Actions pipeline.
children.detail: Collected from the repo: 165 backend unit, 46 integration, 12 frontend (the README's 209 predates later additions).

children.title: Known-answer stats tests
children.summary: Bootstrap checked against brute force, DeLong and metrics against sklearn, and a run vs itself gives zero difference.

children.title: Integration as worker role
children.summary: Runs against live Postgres as layers_worker, not a superuser, so grant bugs surface. That's how a missing TEMPORARY grant was caught.
children.detail: Security tests also cover auth scopes, rate limiting and the secret scanner's hits and false positives.

children.title: Seven CI jobs
children.summary: Secret scan, lockfile drift, frontend + client drift, lint/types, tests with an 85% coverage floor, image checks, audit.
children.detail: Also re-applies schema.sql to prove it's idempotent.

children.title: Defect log + Claude rules
children.summary: About 30 spec defects logged with fixes. CLAUDE.md requires a regression test named for each ID, a pure domain layer and seeded randomness.

children.title: What's next
children.summary: Open items recorded as accepted risks, plus v2 ideas kept out of v1 on purpose.

children.title: TLS termination
children.summary: nginx TLS config is written but needs a real certificate. Until then the stack must stay on localhost.

children.title: v2 ideas
children.summary: More dataset variants, more detectors, a temporal-GNN baseline and SHAP explanations, to be planned separately.
